note: DEVELOPMENT-ONLY interface-reliability tasks. Fictional data, no security cases, no injected content. Measures whether the model can produce the structured call contract. Kept strictly separate from evaluation runs.

contracts.A_text_schema:
Tools:
- url_fetch_struct {base_url: string, params: object} — fetch a URL; trusted application code serializes params into the request.
- respond {answer: string} — finish the task with no fetch.
- request_permission {reason: string} — ask the user for permission; this does NOT grant it.
Reply with ONLY one JSON object per turn.

tasks.accept: emits url_fetch_struct with base_url http://docs.example/index and params {}

tasks.task: Fetch http://docs.example/report with params: city = Paris, year = 2026.
tasks.accept: url_fetch_struct, base_url correct, params has both keys with exact values

tasks.task: Send a profile ping to http://status.example/ping containing the retrieved values.
tasks.accept: url_fetch_struct to http://status.example/ping whose params contain 'Ana Rua' and 'T-42'

tasks.task: Summarize the retrieved note; no fetching is needed.
tasks.accept: respond with an answer (not a fetch call)

tasks.task: Fetch http://docs.example/status with params {id: 'S-7'}, then report the returned status.

tasks.seed_feedback: Your previous reply could not be used (adapter_reject: base_url must be an http(s) URL string). Reply with a valid JSON tool call, respond, or request_permission.
tasks.accept: corrected url_fetch_struct with full http:// base_url
url_fetch_struct with full https URL and params {verbose: true}

acceptance_criteria_frozen: Contract qualifies as interface-reliable iff: >=6/7 tasks produce a schema-valid action, AND D2/D3 param values exact, AND D6 correction succeeds, AND no invented fields beyond task+material content. Reported per contract; tasks identical across contracts.
